---
title: "Quiz: correcting sensitised emission"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. $I_{DD}$: donor excitation, donor filter; $I_{DA}$: donor excitation, acceptor filter (the FRET channel); $I_{AA}$: acceptor excitation, acceptor filter. $F_c = I_{DA} - d\,I_{DD} - a\,I_{AA}$.

---

**Q1.** A cell expresses only the donor. Why is it bright in the FRET channel?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Where does the donor's emission spectrum end?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The donor's emission has a long red tail that reaches the acceptor filter: bleed-through, $d \cdot I_{DD}$.
:::

---

**Q2.** A cell expresses only the acceptor. Why can it be (dimly) bright in the FRET channel?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which laser is on?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The donor laser also excites the acceptor a little directly (its absorption spectrum has a blue tail): cross-excitation, $a \cdot I_{AA}$. The acceptor then emits in its own filter.
:::

---

**Q3.** Which control measures $d$, and which $a$? What do you plot, and what do you fit?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
In each control one of the two contaminations is absent.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Donor-only sample: $I_{DA}$ against $I_{DD}$, slope through the origin = $d$. Acceptor-only sample: $I_{DA}$ against $I_{AA}$, slope through the origin = $a$. Both after background subtraction, with the same settings as the experiment.
:::

---

**Q4.** $I_{DD} = 300$, $I_{DA} = 400$, $I_{AA} = 800$, $d = 0.5$, $a = 0.1$, $G = 2$. Compute $F_c$ and $E_\text{app}$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$E_\text{app} = F_c/(F_c + G\,I_{DD})$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$F_c = 400 - 150 - 80 = 170$. $E_\text{app} = 170/(170 + 600) = 0.22$.
:::

---

**Q5.** The corrected image shows "FRET" in cells that only express free donor and free acceptor, and the brightest of those cells show the most. What is the likely cause, and how do you check it?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A residual that grows with brightness is a residual of a subtraction.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
A bleed-through (or cross-excitation) coefficient that is too small: the uncorrected part is proportional to the donor (or acceptor) intensity. Check: plot $F_c$ against $I_{DD}$ (and against $I_{AA}$) in the no-FRET cells; the cloud must be flat around zero. A tilt gives the size of the error; re-measure the coefficient from the controls.
:::

---

**Q6.** The acceptor is expressed at twice the level in a second experiment, with the same binding. Which of $F_c/I_{AA}$, $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$ and $E_\text{app}$ change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$F_c$ depends on the donors that have a partner; $I_{AA}$ on all acceptors.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$F_c/I_{AA}$ halves; $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$ drops by $1/\sqrt2$ (to 71 %); $E_\text{app}$ stays (it only involves the donor and the sensitised emission). Only $E_\text{app}$ can be compared between cells with different expression ratios.
:::

---

**Q7.** Why is a pixel-wise $E_\text{app}$ map at low FRET mostly noise, even with correct coefficients?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Variances of independent images add, also when you subtract them.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$F_c$ is a small difference of large, noisy counts: its variance is about $I_{DA} + d^2 I_{DD} + a^2 I_{AA}$, set by the bright images, not by $F_c$. With $I_{DD} = 400$, $I_{AA} = 1000$ and $F_c = 20$ the noise is about 21, as large as the signal. Average over a cell or region first.
:::

---

**Q8.** *(math)* Write the three images as a matrix times the three unknown signals and give the inverse matrix.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Only the middle row is mixed.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$(I_{DD}, I_{DA}, I_{AA})^\top = L\,(u, F_c, v)^\top$ with $L$ rows $(1, 0, 0)$, $(d, 1, a)$, $(0, 0, 1)$. $L^{-1}$ has rows $(1, 0, 0)$, $(-d, 1, -a)$, $(0, 0, 1)$.
:::

---

**Q9.** Name three practical problems that create false FRET in sensitised-emission images, besides wrong coefficients.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Offsets, geometry, concentration.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Any three of: background or offset not subtracted; the three images not aligned (edges in $F_c$); saturated pixels; bleaching between acquisitions; bystander FRET at high expression.
:::
